one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event dominates the window: Q3 2026 results and Q4 guidance on 2026-10-29 before the European open (source 3). STM's last seven earnings-day moves were -9%, +7%, -16%, -13%, -6%, +11%, -19% (Yahoo daily, source 13): mean absolute ~11.5%, 5 of 7 negative. Q3 was guided to $3.70B and 37% GM and management already said Q4 revenue 'above $4B' (source 2), so the bar is set; the risk is that Q4 guidance or the GM path disappoints again as in July (stock -18.7% that day), against strong bookings and low channel inventory. The ECB October meeting (Polymarket: hold 90.5%, source 19) is unlikely to move the name. The stock has already fallen 15.6% from $58.72 (Oct 6) to $49.57 and 13.4% from its Oct 2 close ($57.26), about twice SMH's -6.7% from its Oct 2 weekly close to Oct 13 (sources 13, 14), so short-term reversal offsets weak 3-month momentum. I therefore stay near-neutral: median $49.3 (slightly below spot for the negative skew of recent prints), with a fat-tailed spread (mix of 12% and 22% monthly sigma, effective ~17.7%, matching STM's 21-day return sd of 17.7% over 2025-26 and 61%/3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of 15x NTM GAAP EPS at the horizon (~$3.12, mostly FY2028; $46.75, w 0.5), a 4-year DCF at 11.3% WACC and 3% terminal growth ($44.51, w 0.3) and a base-rate anchor of 12-month drift for comparable setups ($49.50, w 0.2) = $46.63, the engine's base horizon value.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount argued as persistent: (1) lower structural profitability - STM's own through-cycle target is 22-24% operating margin vs. TXN/ADI-type analog peers well above that, and its GAAP margin was 1.5% in 2025 (F7/F3); (2) higher capital intensity (net capex ~11.7% of revenue in Q2 2026) and SiC/MCU exposure to Chinese price competition; (3) history: STM ended 2023 at 11.2x and 2024 at 15.0x trailing GAAP EPS, i.e. the market has not paid peer-median multiples near earnings recoveries; (4) customer concentration (Apple) flagged by Barclays' worst case. The multiple is still kept inside the peer range per the rule.

reverse_dcf_check: At 11.3% WACC the DCF gives $44.51; the 15x NTM P/E leg ($46.75) is matched by the DCF at a WACC of ~10.9% (engine reverse DCF). So the horizon multiple implies, after 2028, a ~20% GAAP EBIT margin held for good, ~10% of revenue reinvested as capex, and 3% perpetual growth at ~10.9% cost of capital. That is plausible: it is below STM's 2023 peak margin (26.7%) and its 22-24% through-cycle target, leaving room for the China-competition and Apple risks above; it would not be plausible to assume peer-median 17-20x, which needs the 22-24% model plus lower rates.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT (after SBC) is used throughout; SBC ~1.4% of revenue is an expense, not added back, and the share count falls only ~0.3%/yr (buybacks net of SBC issuance and convertible dilution). Peers' finviz forward P/E is on consensus (largely non-GAAP) EPS, so our GAAP-based 15x is if anything conservative vs. them.

reasoning: Base rates first: STM's own 12-month return since 1997 has a median of ~+1% with a 40% annual sd; pooled analog/semis peers +12.6% (64% up); in the closest analog setup (a >=30% 12-month rally followed by a >=30% drop from the 12-month high, which is where STM sits after running $22->$81 and falling back to $49.6) the pooled peer median was -14% with 42% up, but only ~6 independent episodes and huge dispersion (q10 -52%, q90 +200%). Macro is the main swing factor: Brent ~$125, 10y UST 5.2-5.3%, Fed and ECB still hiking (Polymarket: another Fed hike 79.5%, ECB Dec hike 75%), Hormuz normal by year-end only 13.5%, and a 2027 recession priced at 20% (Kalshi, $673k volume) to 33.5% (Polymarket, thin). The chip upcycle is memory-led and extreme (SIA Aug +144% y/y; WSTS 2027 +27%), while analog grows ~10%. Fundamentals: Q2 revenue +26% y/y, Q3 guide $3.70B/37% GM, Q4 >$4B; consensus 2026/27 revenue $14.4B/$17.2B and EPS $1.35/$2.69. A GAAP model (EBIT margin 8%/14.5%/19%/20% for 2026-29) valued at 15x NTM EPS (inside the 12-peer range, below the 17.4x median for persistent reasons: margins, capital intensity, history of 11-15x) gives $46.75, a DCF at 11.3% gives $44.51, and the base-rate anchor $49.50: fair value $46.63. Scenarios 30/45/25 at $28/$47.5/$74 give a median ~$46.5 and mean ~$48.5; I spread each with ~26-32% sigma so the total log-sd is ~0.45, between STM's 10-year (42%) and 1-year (61%) realized vol. Sell-side mean target $75 is noted but not followed: the July guidance miss (-18.7%) and 5 of 7 negative earnings reactions argue against anchoring on it. Research limited where sites blocked fetching (several news and data pages returned 403/503; sec.gov refused scripted access so filings were read via WebFetch; Twelve Data estimates required a paid plan).
